body:
Source: release review of v1.11.1..main, re-verified on claude-review @ e4b58abe. Defects in packages/backlog-groom:
(a) lib/verify.mjs defaultPathExistsAtHead uses `git cat-file -e`, which accepts a tree; `git show rev:dir` prints a listing, so an excerpt cited against a directory (e.g. `.adlc/manifest.d`) never matches and the issue verifies `fixed` with a non-null contentHash — an actionable close.
(b) lib/content-hash.mjs returns null for the whole issue when any cited path is unreadable, and lib/cache.mjs only refuses `valid` under a null contentHash, so `fixed`/`moved` are cached under an updatedAt-only key; a revert restoring the cited code stays `fixed` on the next cached run.
(c) lib/cluster.mjs unitsForIssue gates on the issue-level verdict and then maps every cited path, including never-existed paths and paths with no excerpt, so an unverified location drives lane clusters, an `area` relabel proposal (lib/relabel.mjs), and the write path's re-derived area move (lib/apply.mjs revalidateRelabel).
(d) lib/fetch.mjs `gh issue list`, the read-path git calls, lib/gh.mjs every writer call, and lib/gate.mjs the reviewer spawn run with no timeout; a stalled remote hangs the sweep, or hangs --apply while it holds the apply lock.
(e) lib/apply.mjs applyRun checks generatedFor and pins reads only when `revision` is truthy; the CLI passes headCommit(), which is null on any git failure, so that run skips the staleness check and reads a moving HEAD.
(f) lib/apply.mjs actionsFromSet accepts `close` from the set's proposals[] with a free-form `field`, which is part of the gate key, so the same close at the same revision can be reviewed again under each new field string.
(g) lib/io.mjs acquireApplyLock's default liveness probe treats EPERM (live process, other uid) as dead and recovers a live lock; its release removes whatever sits at the lock path, so after a lost claim race whose hand-back fails, the original holder's release deletes a third run's live lock.
(h) test/skill-no-direct-mutation.test.mjs matches fixed substrings and misses `gh issue --repo o/r close 7`, `gh api <path> -X PATCH`, and implicit-POST `gh api <path> -f body=...`.
(i) README, apps/docs page, bin header and --help call the package/command read-only while --apply writes; the docs present the one-shot ledger refusal without saying the ledger is gitignored per-checkout state, and present the remote-anchored baseline without saying `origin` is whatever .git/config names. The package is absent from docs/package-reference.md, the README package map and the `adlc` CLI registry, and package.json lists a LICENSE the package does not ship.

CONTEXT FOR THE BUILDER. Package `packages/backlog-groom`: bin/backlog-groom.mjs (CLI; read path and --apply branch), lib/verify.mjs (per-citation verification), lib/git-read.mjs (new: bounded git reads), lib/content-hash.mjs, lib/cache.mjs, lib/cluster.mjs, lib/relabel.mjs, lib/groom.mjs (read pipeline), lib/fetch.mjs, lib/gh.mjs (writer), lib/gate.mjs (reviewer runner), lib/apply.mjs (write run), lib/io.mjs (profile, ledger, apply lock, remote baseline), lib/usage.mjs (help). Tests: `npm test -w packages/backlog-groom` from the worktree root. Existing tests that inject the old `pathExists` seam or call applyRun without a revision are updated in place (seam renamed to `pathKind`; a local wrapper supplies a fixed commit).

NORMATIVE BEHAVIOUR.
1. verifyIssue resolves each citation with `git cat-file -t rev:path` (exported pathKindAtRevision); a non-blob is `unverifiable` with a reason naming the object type. verifyIssue returns `verifiedPaths`: the cited paths whose own check was valid or fixed.
2. unitsForIssue/verifiedLocations use only `verifiedPaths` intersected with the issue's cited paths; a verification with no `verifiedPaths` locates nothing. Area relabel evidence names only those paths.
3. The cache holds a verdict under a null contentHash only if it is `unverifiable` or `unverified`, refused on write and a miss on read; entries carry `verifiedPaths` (validated as a string list); CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION is 3.
4. Every child is bounded with SIGKILL: git reads 30s (lib/git-read.mjs), `gh issue list` 120s (timeout -> `unconsultable`, never an empty backlog), each gh writer call 60s (timeout message names it), the reviewer its --timeout plus 120s (a killed reviewer is 'did not run', never a verdict).
5. applyRun throws an isOpError before any review or write unless `revision` is a 40- or 64-hex commit id; generatedFor is then always required and compared; io is always pinned.
6. proposals[] may carry only `relabel` (PROPOSABLE_ACTIONS); a close is derived only from a `fixed` verdict.
7. Exported pidAlive treats EPERM as alive. The lock records what it wrote; release removes the lock only when its owner record is still this run's. The lock is re-read immediately before a claim; a failed hand-back of a moved live lock is an isOpError naming the moved directory.
8. The SKILL.md guard parses each gh invocation (persistent flags, method anywhere, fields as implicit POST) via test/gh-mutation-matcher.mjs.
9. Documentation: `packages/backlog-groom/README.md` and, by hand, `apps/docs/content/docs/toolkit/backlog-groom.mdx` and `.claude/skills/backlog-groom/SKILL.md` say read-only by default and --apply writes, document --apply/--set and exit codes, state the ledger is per-checkout (a fresh checkout forgets spent reviews) and that `origin` is whatever .git/config names, and name the ledger key as the boundary. `adlc backlog-groom` is registered in packages/cli/lib/registry.mjs (resolved from the workspace like autopilot, no @adlc/cli dependency change); docs/package-reference.md and the root README list the package; packages/backlog-groom/LICENSE exists.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
- AC1 A directory citation is unverifiable, never fixed; pathKindAtRevision reports tree/blob against real git. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/verify-citation-kind.test.mjs`
- AC2 An unverified location drives no cluster, no area relabel, and no write-path area move. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/cluster-per-location.test.mjs`
- AC3 No conclusion about code is cached or served under a null contentHash; a revert is seen on the next cached run. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/cache-code-binding.test.mjs`
- AC4 Every spawn is bounded and a timeout is an ordinary failure. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/spawn-bounds.test.mjs`
- AC5 A non-commit revision refuses before any review or write; a close re-proposed under any field gets no second review. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/apply-authority.test.mjs`
- AC6 EPERM is a live holder; a release never deletes another run's lock; a failed hand-back names the moved directory. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/apply-lock-ownership.test.mjs`
- AC7 The SKILL.md guard catches flag-first, method-last and implicit-POST mutations. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/skill-mutation-matcher.test.mjs packages/backlog-groom/test/skill-no-direct-mutation.test.mjs`
- AC8 Documentation claims match the code on every surface. verify: `node --test packages/backlog-groom/test/docs-claims.test.mjs`
- AC9 Every published package is in the package reference, the README map, and ships its declared LICENSE. verify: `node --test scripts/test/package-reference-coverage.test.mjs`
- AC10 Existing suites green. verify: `npm test -w packages/backlog-groom && npm test -w packages/cli`
- AC11 Mutation gate green on the branch. verify: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0

OUT OF SCOPE: pinning the baseline remote's identity (a new trust anchor); making the gate ledger durable across checkouts; adding @adlc/backlog-groom as an @adlc/cli dependency (package.json/package-lock change); packages/ticket-sync's missing LICENSE (recorded as a shrink-only gap); the concurrent window in which a lock holder whose lock was moved keeps running beside a new holder (now refused loudly, not prevented); the frozen scripts/release-audit-collect.mjs fetch timeout.
title: backlog-groom: verify files only, bound every spawn, harden the apply lock and one-shot key, and document the real trust boundaries
